(you) go / “vas a hacer” = you’re going to do
In questions the voice rises at the end: ¿Quedamos a las tres? ↗. When inviting, Spaniards speak with enthusiasm: ¡Vale! ¡Perfecto!
TR is pronounced with a short tapped r: tren, entrada, otro.
1. The near future: IR A + infinitive
The simplest and most common future in Spanish: the verb IR (which you know from chapter 7) + “a” + infinitive. It works exactly like English “going to…”.
he / she is going to travel
What are you going to do tomorrow?
Don’t forget the “a”: “Voy A estudiar”. “Voy estudiar” is wrong.
You already have a complete future! With “ir a” you can talk about any plan. The “classic” future (viajaré) comes at A2.
2. The verb HACER (to do, to make)
HACER is irregular only in the “yo” form: hago. The rest is regular, like any -er verb.
“Have to” is “tener que” + infinitive. You use conjugated TENER (tengo, tienes…) + “que”.
All four work the same way: conjugated verb + infinitive. With them you can say loads of things with the verbs you already know!
4. Invitations: how to invite, accept and refuse
“Quedar” = to arrange to meet. “¿Quedamos a las seis?” = Shall we meet at six? “¿Dónde quedamos?” = Where shall we meet?
In Spain it’s polite to give a reason when you refuse: “Lo siento, no puedo, tengo que estudiar”.

Los planes de la abuela Rosario
Grandma Rosario is eighty, but she has more energy than her grandchildren.
This Sunday, at the family lunch, she has news: “This summer I’m going on a trip.”
The whole family looks at her. “A trip? Where are you going to go, Mum?”, asks Juan, Ana’s father.
“I’m going to Mexico to visit my brother Manuel. I haven’t seen him for twenty years.”
Carmen, Ana’s mother, is worried: “But it’s a very long journey. It’s eleven hours by plane.”
“I know,” answers Grandma. “I’m going to take a book, my pills and a little cushion to sleep on.”
Lucía has an idea: “Grandma, do you want company? I’m on holiday in July. I can go with you!”.
Grandma smiles. “Of course, dear. But you have to learn a bit of Mexican history.”
Then everyone starts making plans. Pablo is going to look for the tickets online.
Ana is going to buy a new suitcase for Grandma, because hers is from 1985.
Mihai, being a doctor, is going to prepare a list of medicines for the trip.
“And what are you going to do in Mexico?”, asks Mihai.
“First we’re going to stay with my brother and his family. Then we’re going to visit the pyramids and eat tacos every day,” says Grandma.
“And we’re going to dance!”, adds Lucía. Everyone laughs. It’s going to be an unforgettable summer.
That night, Grandma can’t sleep. She’s very happy. She opens her wardrobe and starts packing… in June, a month early!
